content.title: The Bachelorette Season 22: What to Know About the Canceled Season Starring Taylor Frankie Paul
content.text: NEED TO KNOW In September 2025, Taylor Frankie Paul was announced as the next lead of The BachelorettePaul's season of The Bachelorette was originally set to premiere on March 22, but was canceled by ABC three days priorThe cancelation came after TMZ published a 2023 video showing the reality star throwing chairs at her ex-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen Taylor Frankie Paul's season of The Bachelorette has been canceled. The reality star — who has been part of Hulu's The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives since 2024 — announced in a Sept. 10 interview on Call Her Daddy that she would star in the upcoming season of ABC's The Bachelorette. Ultimately, Paul's journey won't be shown on TV. On March 19, ABC canceled her already-filmed season of The Bachelorette after TMZ published a 2023 video showing the reality star throwing chairs at her ex-boyfriend, Dakota Mortensen, in front of her daughter. “Taylor is very grateful for ABC’s support as she prioritizes her family’s safety and security,” a spokesperson for The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star said in a statement obtained by PEOPLE. The statement continued, “After years of silently suffering extensive mental and physical abuse as well as threats of retaliation, Taylor is finally gaining the strength to face her accuser and taking steps to ensure that she and her children are protected from any further harm." Dakota also spoke out in a statement to PEOPLE, saying, "As anyone who has seen the video will understand, this is a deeply upsetting situation. I am, unfortunately, used to these baseless claims about me and our relationship, which I categorically deny. I am focusing on our son and his safety, and hope that Taylor will do the same." Here's everything to know about Taylor Frankie Paul's The Bachelorette season 22, which has since been canceled. Who was season 22's Bachelorette? Taylor Frankie Paul. Cristian Lopez/Disney via Getty Paul's involvement on The Bachelorette initially began as a joke on TikTok — one that she's not sure if the producers ever saw — and she was shocked when she got the invitation. "I don't know if that got their attention," Paul told Alex Cooper in a September 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "It was mainly a joke to me ... then we had a meeting. I still didn't believe it until I got the invitation, 'Will you be our Bachelorette?' Same reaction, shaking, pacing back and forth. There's no way, no way." Since 2024, Paul has starred in the hit Hulu reality series The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives alongside her fellow MomTok group, who rose to fame on TikTok for their infamous soft-swinging scandal. She shares two kids, Indy May Paul and Ocean Paul, with her ex-husband, Tate Paul, and a son with Mortensen named Ever True Mortensen. Where was The Bachelorette season 22 filmed? The Bachelor Mansion. Juliana Yamada / Los Angeles Times via Getty ABC never officially announced the filming locations for The Bachelorette season 22. However, Paul said on Call Her Daddy that her reservations about saying yes were tied to being away from her home in Utah. "I'm a co-parent," she told Cooper. "I have two baby daddies, not one, so I'm dealing with two different people, my children, my home base is here. Can I travel that long? Can I be gone that long?" Parts of the series were filmed in Utah, according to Axios. In November 2025, the show filmed in Colorado, per The Denver Post. Who were the contestants? 'The Bachelorette' season 19. Craig Sjodin/ABC via Getty In February 2026, ABC announced the full lineup of contestants who were set to appear on Paul's season of The Bachelorette. Related Stories Among the contestants was Lana Del Rey's former fiancé, Clayton Johnson. The couple dated in 2020 and sources confirmed to PEOPLE that they were engaged that December, but it's not clear when they broke up. Why was The Bachelorette season 22 canceled? Taylor Frankie Paul. Santiago Felipe/Getty The Bachelorette season 22 was set to premiere on March 22, 2026, but it was canceled three days ahead of its release on March 19. Following TMZ releasing a 2023 video that showed Paul throwing metal chairs at Mortensen while one of her children was nearby, ABC announced that they would not be moving forward with airing her season of the show. “In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of The Bachelorette at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family," a statement from a Disney Entertainment Television spokesperson read.
